data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A merely compliant checklist is fragile under distribution shift; a genuinely reliable checklist is robust.","Compliance can be achieved without understanding; reliability requires structural alignment with the task's causal model.","A compliant checklist may fail adversarial perturbations; a reliable one should resist them."],"overturn_conditions":["If OOD cases are not feasible to construct or evaluate within the task domain.","If the task is so simple or narrow that OOD cases are indistinguishable from in-distribution cases.","If expert intuition and checklist compliance fail equally on OOD cases, OOD does not discriminate between them."],"shared_structure":["Both a merely compliant checklist and a genuinely reliable checklist map inputs to outputs.","Both can achieve high accuracy on an in-distribution evaluation set.","Both can be evaluated against an objective outcome metric."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001","SRC_002","SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["From machine learning generalization theory: OOD performance distinguishes causal model acquisition from spurious correlation learning.","From causal inference: interventions on surface features that preserve the causal structure can reveal whether a model relies on true causal links."]},"claim":"To distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer, the critical evidence within a single evaluation is whether the panel outperforms on out-of-distribution (OOD) or adversarial cases where superficial checklist heuristics fail but the underlying causal structure remains the same. Genuine reliability gain implies the checklist has captured the causal structure of the task; mere compliance implies the checklist tracks surface correlates that can be gamed or disrupted.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the task distribution is narrow and stable (no meaningful OOD cases exist), the distinction between compliance and genuine gain is practically irrelevant.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If expert intuition also relies on surface correlations rather than causal structure, OOD cases may not distinguish panel from expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist is so tightly coupled to the training distribution that it cannot generalize, but the task itself does not require generalization, the distinction is moot.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mere compliance is a mapping from input features to outputs that exploits correlations in the training distribution. Genuine reliability gain is a mapping that exploits the causal structure generating the outcomes. If the checklist encodes causal structure, it will remain reliable under interventions or distribution shifts that preserve the causal structure but alter surface correlations. If the checklist encodes only surface compliance, it will fail under such shifts. Thus, OOD test cases that decorrelate surface features from causal structure form the critical discriminating evidence.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
